project.name: Proven
project.summary: A pull-request reviewer whose every finding carries evidence a reader can check again: a test that fails on the change, or a query through Zetaris and the rows it returned.

track: The Agent That Can Explain Why

builders.name: Marcin "Wato" Marzec
builders.role: owner: decides and merges; writes no code

zetaris.how: The evidence layer: the Investigator proves a finding about a dependency with one SQL query over REST and the rows it returned (CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS, OSV by advisory id). In sample mode the same SQL runs over local sample tables shaped like the Zetaris views; live Zetaris evidence in a review is next.

meterless.how: H-MEM remembers findings refuted in earlier reviews, so they do not come back; the World Model holds the entities a review has seen, and its ingest survives a kill and a restart. Both are a minimum in Go, checked with Meterless's own conformance suites (H-MEM 9 of 13, World Model 7 of 8; the failures are the sections not built yet). Every model call goes through Meterless Nightshift, and the answering model is read from its signed receipt.

cursor.how: Cursor agents write Proven's product code: up to four at once, headless on a Linux machine, each from a signed order, in its own copy of the repository, inside a jail with its own network and an egress door, and with every model request recorded by a proxy. 16 changes were merged on day one.

nvidia.how: Nemotron answers Proven's agents through Meterless Nightshift, and the Skeptic that tries to refute each finding defaults to Nemotron; an answer that did not come from an NVIDIA model is refused by name. Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety checks every prompt and every answer, on our own model server or through NVIDIA's hosted API.

pre_existing.name: Saphan Studio
pre_existing.what: The platform that runs the agent fleet building Proven: orders, runs, reviews and their record. A tool used to build, not part of the product.

pre_existing.name: Test corpus
pre_existing.what: 21 test-case contracts from 28 real review disagreements, declared as prior art; their executable tests are written inside the build window.
